clinicalPearls: Overdose typically causes profound central nervous system and respiratory depression, hypotonia and coma, often requiring airway protection and ventilation
The depth of coma can mimic a devastating neurological event, including loss of brainstem reflexes, yet is usually reversible with supportive care
Paradoxically, seizures can occur despite baclofen being a central nervous system depressant
Bradycardia and hypotension, or occasionally hypertension and tachycardia, may accompany the toxidrome
There is no specific antidote, so management is meticulous supportive and intensive care with airway control and ventilation as needed
Recovery may be prolonged, particularly in renal impairment or after large ingestions, so a normal appearance should not prompt premature extubation or discharge

Abrupt cessation, especially failure of an intrathecal pump, causes a dangerous withdrawal syndrome with rebound spasticity, hyperthermia, autonomic instability and delirium that can be life-threatening
Baclofen withdrawal can resemble severe sepsis, serotonin syndrome or neuroleptic malignant syndrome and is treated by urgently restoring baclofen and providing supportive care
reference.pathophysiology: Baclofen is a structural analogue of the inhibitory neurotransmitter gamma-aminobutyric acid and acts as an agonist at gamma-aminobutyric-acid type B receptors, predominantly in the spinal cord, reducing excitatory neurotransmission and muscle tone. In overdose, excessive receptor stimulation causes marked central nervous system depression, hypotonia, respiratory depression and coma, with cardiovascular effects and a lowered seizure threshold in some patients. Baclofen is largely renally eliminated, so impaired renal function prolongs and intensifies toxicity. Sudden withdrawal removes chronic inhibitory tone, producing a hyperexcitable rebound state with severe spasticity and autonomic dysregulation.
additionalDifferentials: For withdrawal: sepsis, serotonin syndrome, neuroleptic malignant syndrome or malignant hyperthermia
additionalInvestigations: Arterial blood gas and continuous oxygen saturation to assess ventilation
Renal function and electrolytes, given renal elimination
Electrocardiogram for bradycardia and conduction disturbance
Creatine kinase and temperature monitoring, particularly in withdrawal
Neuroimaging if a structural cause of coma cannot be excluded
redFlags: Respiratory depression or apnoea requiring airway support
Deep coma with loss of brainstem reflexes
Suspected intrathecal pump failure or withdrawal with hyperthermia and autonomic instability
reference.prognosis: Overdose generally has a good prognosis with supportive care and mechanical ventilation, with full neurological recovery even after profound coma, though recovery may be slow in renal impairment; unrecognised withdrawal, especially from intrathecal therapy, can be fatal.
pitfalls: Mistaking reversible deep coma with absent brainstem reflexes for irreversible brain injury
Extubating or discharging prematurely before prolonged effects resolve
Overlooking impaired renal clearance that prolongs toxicity
Failing to recognise and urgently treat baclofen withdrawal
Attributing withdrawal to sepsis or another hyperthermic syndrome and delaying baclofen restoration
management: No specific antidote exists, so management centres on meticulous supportive and intensive care
Secure the airway and provide mechanical ventilation for respiratory depression and coma
Support the circulation with intravenous fluids and vasoactive agents for hypotension, and treat symptomatic bradycardia
Consider haemodialysis to enhance elimination in severe poisoning with renal impairment, given the drug's renal clearance
In abrupt withdrawal, especially from intrathecal therapy, urgently reinstate baclofen and control autonomic instability and rebound spasticity with benzodiazepines
Avoid premature extubation or discharge as recovery may be prolonged, monitoring renal function, temperature and creatine kinase
